summary:
AgroSmart is an intelligent web platform designed to help farmers in Andahuaylas, Apurímac, Peru, make better agricultural decisions in response to climate change. It integrates NASA POWER climate data to display temperature, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation through interactive maps and charts.
The platform allows users to select their farmland on an interactive map, identify its geographic location, and estimate its altitude above sea level. By combining altitude, climate conditions, and soil characteristics, AgroSmart evaluates crop suitability and recommends crops adapted to each plot's specific conditions.
Users can also register soil properties, select crops, and define agricultural priorities. The system compares crop rotation alternatives, providing suitability scores, alerts, and explanations to support informed decisions.
AgroSmart promotes sustainable agriculture through efficient water use, soil conservation, and better adaptation to changing climate conditions. By combining NASA POWER data and geographic information, the platform transforms environmental data into practical tools that support farmers in our region.
details:
What exactly does the project do?

AgroSmart is a web platform designed to support agricultural decision-making. Its main objective is to help farmers understand the climate, altitude, and soil conditions of their land so they can identify suitable crops and plan crop rotation alternatives.

The system allows users to:

  • Access climate information for a specific location through NASA POWER.
  • Visualize climate information through interactive maps and charts.
  • Monitor variables such as temperature, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation.
  • Identify the estimated altitude of an agricultural plot based on its geographical coordinates.
  • Evaluate which crops are suitable for the altitude and environmental conditions of each plot.
  • Register the soil characteristics of an agricultural plot.
  • Select crops and establish priorities based on farmers' needs.
  • Compare crop rotation alternatives using suitability scores and agricultural criteria.
  • Display alerts and explanations to help users understand the results.

How does it work?

The platform operates through six main stages:

  1. Agricultural Area Selection: The user selects or identifies the location of their land on an interactive map, focusing on agricultural areas in the province of Andahuaylas.
  2. Altitude Identification: Using the geographical coordinates of the selected plot, the platform obtains its estimated altitude above sea level. This information helps identify the elevation conditions of the agricultural area.
  3. Climate Data Collection: The platform accesses NASA POWER to obtain temperature, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation data based on the selected location and time period.
  4. Agricultural Suitability Evaluation: The system combines the estimated altitude, available climate information, and registered soil characteristics to evaluate which crops are more suitable for the selected plot. This helps identify crops that are better adapted to the environmental conditions of each location.
  5. Agricultural Information Registration: Farmers enter the characteristics of their soil, select the crops they are interested in, and establish their priorities, such as water conservation, soil preservation, or productivity.
  6. Comparison of Alternatives: The system uses the available information to compare different crop rotation options and provides suitability scores, alerts, and explanations to guide farmers' decisions.

What are its benefits?

  • Agricultural Benefits: Helps farmers identify suitable crops according to the altitude, climate conditions, and soil characteristics of their land. It also supports crop selection and rotation planning.
  • Environmental Benefits: Promotes responsible water use, soil fertility conservation, and more sustainable agricultural practices.
  • Technological Benefits: Provides easier access to NASA scientific information and geographical elevation data through interactive maps, charts, and user-friendly tools.
  • Social Benefits: Aims to support farmers in Andahuaylas, especially those who need information to identify crops adapted to their local conditions, manage climate variations, and reduce risks in their agricultural activities.

What do we expect to achieve?

In the short term, we aim to develop and demonstrate a functional prototype that allows users to access climate information from NASA POWER, visualize climate variables, identify the estimated altitude of their agricultural land, register soil characteristics, and receive crop recommendations based on the altitude, climate, and soil conditions of their plots. The platform will also allow users to compare crop rotation alternatives.

In the long term, we hope that the platform can become a useful decision-support tool for farmers in Apurímac and other regions of Peru facing changing climate conditions. Our purpose is to contribute to more sustainable agriculture, improve crop planning, help farmers select crops better adapted to their land, and encourage the use of scientific and geographical data to make better decisions in the field.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, and software did we use?

Web Development (Frontend):

  • HTML5: Used to structure the platform.
  • CSS3: Used to design and style the interface.
  • JavaScript ES6+: Used to implement the functionality and interactions of the platform.

Maps and Data Visualization:

  • Leaflet.js: Used to create interactive maps and allow users to select their agricultural plots.
  • Chart.js: Used to display climate information through charts.

NASA Data Sources:

  • NASA POWER: Used to obtain meteorological and solar data.

Geographical Elevation Data:

  • Open-Meteo Elevation API: Used to obtain estimated terrain elevation based on the geographical coordinates of the selected plot.

Development and Programming Tools:

  • Visual Studio Code: Code editor used for development.
  • Web Browser: Used to test and visualize the platform.
  • Git and GitHub: Used for version control and code storage, if implemented by the team.

Programming Languages:

  • HTML5.
  • CSS3.
  • JavaScript.

Hardware:

  • Computers and laptops used for software development and system testing.

Information Sources:

  • Climate and meteorological data from NASA POWER.
  • Geographical elevation data used to estimate the altitude of agricultural plots.
  • Agricultural information and soil characteristics collected or registered for the project.

In what way is our project creative?

The creativity of our project lies in integrating NASA scientific information, geographical elevation data, and agricultural needs in our region. Unlike platforms that only display weather information, AgroSmart considers the altitude of each agricultural plot, together with its climate conditions and soil characteristics, to evaluate which crops are more suitable for that specific location.

This approach allows the platform to provide different crop recommendations depending on the elevation and environmental conditions of each plot. For example, a crop that may be suitable for a lower-altitude area is not automatically recommended for a higher-altitude area.

Furthermore, we present the results through maps, charts, suitability scores, and simple explanations, transforming scientific and geographical data into practical information that farmers can use to plan their agricultural activities.

What factors did our team consider?

To develop our proposal, our team considered the following factors:

  • Climate Conditions: Variations in temperature, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation that may affect crops.
  • Altitude: The elevation of each agricultural plot above sea level, which influences the environmental conditions and the suitability of different crops.
  • Soil Characteristics: Soil texture, pH, fertility, drainage, and water availability.
  • Geographical Location: The different environmental and agricultural conditions of the province of Andahuaylas.
  • Crop Adaptability: The ability of different crops and varieties to grow under specific altitude, climate, and soil conditions.
  • Farmers' Needs: The importance of providing clear and useful information to support decision-making.
  • Data Reliability: The use of scientific sources and the identification of missing or estimated information.
  • Ease of Use: A simple interface that allows users to access maps, charts, and results without requiring advanced technical knowledge.
  • Agricultural Sustainability: The importance of conserving water, protecting soil, and promoting agriculture that is better prepared for climate variations.
